question.problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -9 & 0 \\ 4 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Determine whether $A=PD{P}^{-1}$ for some invertible matrix $P$ and a diagonal matrix $D,$ where $P$ and $D$ are both real. In the affirmative case, find a possible diagonal matrix $D.$

current_example.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine whether $D$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb R.$ 

We start by computing the eigenvalues of $A.$ To do that, we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 6 & 0 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & -4 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 6 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )([{\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +2]-12) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda -10) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )(\lambda -5)(\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues of $A$ are $\lambda_1=4,$ $\lambda_2=5,$ and $\lambda_3=-2.$ Since all of the eigenvalues are simple roots of the characteristic polynomial, $A$ is diagonalizable. 

We construct a diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal. Therefore, one possible matrix $D$ is
